content.title: Space in Flow
content.hook: You already know the box model. Now use it as a layout tool.
content.context:
Padding creates space inside a box. Margin creates space outside a box.

In ordinary flow, that space changes how much room an element and its neighbors need.
goals: Use padding and margin deliberately in a flowing layout and predict how added space changes nearby content.

options.text: Space is added outside each paragraph, separating it from following content.

feedback.correct: Margin is outside the box. A bottom margin changes the space between that paragraph and what follows it.
feedback.incorrect: Margin is outside the box. A bottom margin changes the space between that paragraph and what follows it.

content.question:
A card needs more breathing room between its border and its text.

Which is the more direct tool?

options.text: Either one always means the same thing.

feedback.correct: Padding is inside the box. It creates space between the content and the border.
feedback.incorrect: Padding is inside the box. It creates space between the content and the border.

activities.title: Tiny lab
activities.instruction: Compose your response below, then submit to compare with the reference guide.

content.prompt:
Create two stacked cards.

Give the first card padding.

Give the second card a bottom margin.

Look carefully at the two kinds of space.

Ask yourself:

**“Is the space inside the box, or between boxes?”**
guidelines: State your reasoning clearly in your own words or code.
Compare your response with the reference guide after submitting.
content.sampleResponse: Review your explanation against the core mental model of this lesson.

feedback.correct: Review your explanation against the core mental model of this lesson.
feedback.incorrect: Please write a brief response (at least 10 characters) before submitting.

content.question: If you double the bottom margin of the first card, what should happen to the second card's starting position?

feedback.correct: More outside space after the first card pushes the following content farther away in normal flow.
feedback.incorrect: More outside space after the first card pushes the following content farther away in normal flow.

content.title: A useful anti-habit
content.text:
Do not use margin as a blind “move this thing 12px to the right” button.

First describe the relationship you need.

- Space inside a component → padding.
- Space between nearby components → margin.
- Later, when you learn layout systems, some relationships can be expressed even more directly.

content.question: You want text farther from a card's border but do not want to increase the gap between that card and the next card. Which property is the more direct tool?

feedback.correct: Padding changes internal space. Margin changes external space.
feedback.incorrect: Padding changes internal space. Margin changes external space.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** Padding is internal breathing room; margin is external spacing.
**Senior habit:** Describe the space problem before choosing the property.
**Mastery signal:** You can predict how a margin or padding change affects nearby content without trial-and-error nudging.
